main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snowy roof slope (rows ~8-35) above a log front wall with a door and two shuttered windows (rows ~38-62)
top_band: Roof snow in white and pale blue, rows ~8-35 (the lightest tone), ending in a lighter snow eave edge at rows ~31-35 with icicles below
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: the snowy roof slope fills rows 8-35 as a large foreshortened top surface. The roof ends in a thick snow eave at rows 31-35. Dark eave shadow and icicles sit at rows 36-39. Below that is the log wall front with a door and windows, rows 40-62. The windows have blue shutters and dark frames, and the door has a frame with iron bands, so they read as inset. A roof slope plus a front wall matches the 3/4 building structure.

style.evidence: The snow has about 4-5 steps (white, pale blue, blue-grey, shadow blue) with scalloped drift shadows. The wood has about 4-5 browns with log ends and plank grain. The outlines are dark brown or dark blue, tinted to the neighbouring material rather than neutral black. The windows have glow gradients, and there are icicles, a stone chimney and branches. The upper roof snow is quite smooth, so the piece is a little lighter in texture than the tile-roof reference. Overall it is acceptable beside the references.
